title: The Evening Brief: Markets sink as whale exodus and regulatory pressure mount
dek: Sunday closes a week of heavy selling and accumulation moves: spot Bitcoin ETFs saw outflows on the day while whales pulled over $2.2 billion in bitcoin off exchanges in the week ending Nov 8. Fear gauge sits at 28.
author: GoCheckMyCrypto
key_fact: Bitcoin down 0.94% over 24 hours and down 2.25% over seven days as the week's whale outflows signal accumulation, yet ETF flows turned negative on the day and remain underwater for the week, creating a split signal between institutional and self-custody behavior.
bottom_line: Bitcoin down 0.94% over 24 hours and down 2.25% over seven days as the desk's Whale Watch board showed $2.292 billion in bitcoin moving off exchanges during the week ending Nov 08, a pattern of accumulation that contradicts spot Bitcoin ETF outflows of $411.9M on the day and $1,281.7M over the week. Technical indicators show deep oversold conditions across major assets: Bitcoin's RSI at 35.8, Ether at 34.0, Cardano at 25.4. The Fear and Greed Index closed at 28. No near-term regulatory or market checkpoints are stated in the desk's coverage, but whale positioning and funding dynamics warrant close watching in the days ahead.
body: The crypto market closed Sunday with broad weakness and fragmented capital flows. Bitcoin down 0.94% over 24 hours, Ether down 3.62% over 24 hours, and most large-cap coins sinking across all timeframes.

The week ending Nov 8 saw $2,292M in bitcoin move off exchanges, per the desk's Whale Watch board, extending a larger pattern: the week ending Nov 01 saw $4,829M move off exchanges, and the week ending Oct 18 saw $205M move off. This pattern of accumulation into self-custody addresses suggests whales treated selloffs as entry points. Yet spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of $411.9M on the day, November 6, and outflows of $1,281.7M over the week through November 6, a reversal from the cumulative $55.766 billion in spot Bitcoin ETF net inflows recorded to date. Ether spot ETFs showed outflows of $93.3 million on Nov 6 and $365.2 million over the last five sessions, against cumulative inflows of $11.951 billion.

On the leverage side, OKX funding rates remained calm. Open interest in Bitcoin on OKX stood at $2.536 billion, with a long-to-short ratio of 2.87, indicating heavy long positioning. XRP's ratio was most extreme at 4.24, Dogecoin at 5.36. Liquidations over the past hour tilted toward long-side pain in XRP and Dogecoin, where $1.591 million and $631.4 thousand in longs were cleared, respectively; Ether saw only short-side liquidations of $374.9 thousand.

Technically, the desk's boards show persistent oversold conditions. Bitcoin's RSI sat at 35.8, Ether at 34.0, Solana at 27.5, Cardano at 25.4, all in deep fear territory. Yet Bitcoin held above its 200-day moving average and maintained a golden cross; BNB, XRP, Solana, ADA, and DOGE all showed golden crosses despite trading below their 200-day lines. Bitcoin trades 40% below its 12-month high of $124,739.81; Ether 54.3% below $4,690.84; Cardano 79.9% below $0.8744. The broader Fear and Greed Index closed at 28, in the Fear band.

Totalcrypto market cap stood at $2.491 trillion, with Bitcoin dominance at 60.2%. Stablecoins supply fell 4.37% over the past 30 days to $293.261 billion. PEPE led daily gainers with an increase of 3.54% over 24 hours; M, PI, and STX were the largest losers, down 6.73%, 6.38%, and 6.35% respectively over 24 hours.
